chapter: Teachers: Preston Jackson and Roy Palmer
title: Studying with Roy Palmer
summary: Wynn describes Roy Palmer as a natural technician and teacher who dressed carelessly, played trumpet and led a brass band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: The technique that man had was just terrific.

I mean, he was just a natural traumas. So I finished up my studying with Roy. I went to Roy. Roy was just like Preston. I mean, he was just interested in kids and youngsters and he tried to pass on all his knowledge to me. But what year was that then when you studied the floor? That was probably in the early 20, in 21 or 22, somewhere around in there. Roy was a terrific technician on that floor.
He didn't make very many records. He made a few though, and you can hear him on some of them.

Yeah, the fellows used to say that, I never know if it would be a fact or something, but they used to say Roy was very lazy. They would say that he would come on a job and play like the Dickens probably for about 45 minutes and then he was ready to go to sleep or anything. Yeah, I heard that. But he was playing while he was playing. Yeah. And Roy was a fellow. I mean, I know this to be a fact that he didn't care anything about appearance. In those days bands used to wear tuxedas and whatnot. And I never will forget Roy used to come up to work. I remember several occasions I'd go around and wear his work. And then he had a tuxedo. It had turned green, the original color probably was black. I had one too. And he just soon put on a green shirt with a tuxedo. He was just that type, he was just what he was.
He used to work in the daytime too as a mechanic and all. I guess he'd be sleepy on a job. Yeah, and then he had quite a few kids.

I mean, Roy was a wonderful musician. I mean, it was fascinating to see how he could teach all those instruments. I mean, a lot of times I would go there early, you know. This time he would be teaching drums. And to my way of thinking now was correctly. I mean, he could pick up a drumstick and make it a beautiful, perfect roll. He could actually show you what he wanted you to do. That's the one thing that most of those teachers were like Mr. Jackson. He couldn't show you on your instrument how it should be done.

And just as good as he was on trombone. That's just as sad as he was on trumpet to my idea of thinking. His ideas on trumpet were very corny. I mean, my way of thinking. And he loved the trumpet. The trumpet was really his love. And after I got so that I could play, he had a marching band, a brass band around there. So he'd always put me on the trombone and he would play the trumpet. And I just didn't like his trumpet playing at all. It was really ratatirous, you know. But he had a terrific pair of lips. I mean, he could, for endurance and range, he had it all.
